svg.title: Adiabatic mixing of H2SO4 and water to 40 wt% on the H–x chart
svg.text: Mixing H₂SO₄ (27 °C) with water (27 °C) to 40 wt%: final temperature
H–x diagram for H₂SO₄/H₂O (SVNA Fig. 12.17, attached to the paper), redrawn; right: zoom around the 40% line
Mark water at 27 °C on the x = 0 axis (H = 113.2 kJ/kg) and pure acid at 27 °C on x = 100 (H ≈ 2.8 kJ/kg).
Join them: adiabatic mixing lies on this straight line. At 40 wt% it gives M: H = 0.4(2.8) + 0.6(113.2) = 69 kJ/kg.
Go up the 40% line: the 100 °C isotherm is at ≈ 16 and the dotted boiling line at ≈ 50 kJ/kg; M is on/just above it.
So the solution reaches its boiling point: T ≈ 113 °C (between the 110 °C isotherm and the boiling line).
Isotherms are 10–15 °C apart (−20, 0, 10, 25, 40 … 140 °C); in the zoom: blue = 100 and 110 °C, red dotted = boiling line.
Redrawn from SVNA Fig. 12.17 (digitized curves); in the exam read the printed chart — values may differ slightly.
